title: Alerts routing & escalation — backlog notes and wireframe sketched
content:
Context / goal:
- Goal: design a lightweight, extensible alerting UI in Console that surfaces SLO breaches and operational anomalies, lets teams configure routing/escalation policies per-service/model/route, and reduces noise using confidence scoring and grouping.
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, product owners for hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Constraints: must work with existing backend routing (routing policies + webhooks), integrate with PagerDuty/Slack/Email, and support per-customer overrides for Dedicated/Private.

Quick summary of the idea (elevator):
- Alerts center: single place showing active incidents + historical alerts + quiet windows.
- Policy builder: visual editor to create channel routing + escalation paths + suppression rules.
- Noise controls: alert confidence (signal score), auto-grouping, dedupe window, and prediction-based suppression for transient spikes.
- SLO linkage: one-click view from an SLO to its alerting policy; show how many alerts came from each SLO slice.

Wireframe sketches (textual):
- Topbar: "Alerts" | filter dropdown (team / service / model / severity) | quick create policy button (+)
- Left column (30%):
  - Active incidents (compact list) with chips: [sev:P0] [route:api-1] [customers:global]
  - Quick filters: P0/P1, Unacked, Recently Resolved
- Main column (70%):
  - Incident detail pane (when selected): title, timeline, implicated routes/models, last 72h sample traces, suggested runbook links, current routing policy (editable inline)
  - Bottom of detail: actions -> Ack / Reassign / Escalate / Silence (duration) / Create ticket
- Policy builder modal: three columns: triggers -> routing -> escalation
  - triggers: choose metric (p99 latency, error rate, e2e failure rate, token failure), comparator, window, sensitivity slider (aggressive|balanced|lenient)
  - routing: channels (Slack, Email, Webhook, PagerDuty, Opsgenie), oncall schedule selector, per-channel delay (e.g., post to Slack immediately, wait 2m then PagerDuty)
  - escalation: chain editor with timeout and fallback (if no ack in X minutes -> next channel/role), also per-customer severity multiplier

Backlog grooming notes (prioritized):
1) BACKLOG-21: Basic Alerts center list + incident detail (MVP) - UX + frontend + minimal backend endpoints (list, acknowledge, silence). Acceptance criteria: filter by team, show last 3 events, ack/unack flows complete. (Owner: Asha)
2) BACKLOG-22: Policy builder v1 (triggers + Slack/webhook routing). Acceptance: create/edit/delete policy, attach to SLO. (Owner: Priya)
3) BACKLOG-23: Escalation chains + oncall schedule integration (read-only) - must map to PagerDuty. Acceptance: chain executes in simulated environment. (Owner: Diego)
4) BACKLOG-37: Noise controls: confidence scoring + dedupe window, default for new policies = enabled. Acceptance: reduce duplicate alerts by 60% on test traffic. (Owner: Evan)
5) BACKLOG-51: Per-customer overrides and Dedicated/Private visibility rules. Acceptance: customers on Dedicated can have policy locked to account admins. (Owner: Product-Eng lead)

Notes / design decisions to confirm:
- Signal score: generate an internal 0-100 score based on: magnitude of breach vs baseline, trend persistence, cross-region agreement. Use for suppression thresholds (e.g., only fire alerts if score >= 40).
- Grouping: group alerts by root cause candidate (model+route+error code) using 10m lookback of correlated traces. UX should show grouping rationale.
- SLO-based alert triggers vs raw metric triggers: expose both; default SLO alerts map to burn-rate alarms but allow raw metric policies.
- Notification templates: include contextual snippets (last user query sample sanitized, token counts, cost delta) for high-cost anomalies.
- Mute windows: team-level schedule + policy-level temporary silences. Silences should show who created them and have audit links.

Unresolved questions (to bring to stakeholders):
- Who owns escalation policies for multi-team services? Product or Platform SRE? Propose: service owner owns policy; platform provides templates.
- Default thresholds per model family — can we suggest sensible starting points? Need data from serving runtime on latencies per model.
- How to represent per-tenant policies in Hosted: separate policy copies or policy with tenant-scoped overrides?

Edge cases we must support:
- Cross-region partial degradations: if region A has issues but region B fine, route alerts to regional oncall unless global impact > X% users.
- Model rollouts: allow temporary higher tolerance during rollouts (rollout window mode)
- API rate-limits causing backpressure: coalesce token-throttle errors into one incident with guidance to increase concurrency.

Example policy pseudo-spec (for backend team):
- name: "P99 latency - text-gen - model-x"
- trigger: metric(p99_latency, route=text-gen, model=model-x) > 1500ms for 3m
- signal_score_threshold: 50
- dedupe_key: concat(model, route, error_class)
- actions: [ {channel: slack, target: #infra-alerts, delay: 0}, {channel: pagerduty, schedule: pd-service-x, delay: 120} ]
- escalation: [ {after: 5m, action: pusher(pagerduty, schedule: pd-service-x-team2)} ]

Suggested UX text snippets (for copywriter):
- "Muted for 30m by @name — reason: deploying canary"
- "Policy: P99 latency - model-x — triggered 3 times in last hour"
- "Suggested runbook: Increase replica count -> enable caching -> revert last model change"

Operational playbook pointers (link in UI):
- Runbook: /confluence/ops/alerts/runbooks/p99-latency
- PagerDuty mapping doc: /confluence/ops/esc/pd-mapping

Testing notes / metrics for rollout:
- Success metrics: time-to-ack (median) < 5m for P1; false-positive rate decrease by 40% after noise controls enabled.
- Telemetry to add: alert_fired_reason, dedupe_group_id, signal_score, policy_id, ack_latency_ms

Implementation risks & mitigation:
- Risk: policy complexity -> users create many policies and confusion. Mitigate: provide templates and a policy analyzer that warns about overlaps.
- Risk: webhook churn with many destinations. Mitigate: central webhook proxy + retry/backoff.

Next steps (owners & short timeboxes):
- This week: finalize the top-level wireframe and agree canonical policy fields (Asha + Priya) - 3d
- Next week: spike on signal_score algorithm using 7 days of prod metrics (Evan) - 5d
- 2 sprints: deliver MVP Alerts center + basic policy CRUD + Slack integration (Team: console + backend)

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep policy editor modal minimal to start; advanced boolean logic later.
- Make UI show "Policy suggestion" from historical incidents (ML-driven) — future backlog item.
- Add "quiet mode" button in topbar for maintenance windows.
